content:
Marissa Cole: PRD pass on Safe apply + rollback. I want to align on UX expectations for “one-click rollback” + customer-facing wording. Also: do we require justification (ticket link) on rollback, or just permission-gated?

Kenji Nakamura: +1. “One-click” in UX usually means: single primary action from history screen, but still confirmation modal. We should be precise in wording.

Paula Mendes: From rollout/telemetry POV: we should always capture *reason* (free text) + optional ticket link. Otherwise audit log is weak and support investigations are painful.

Dylan Brooks: Engineering POV: adding a required text box is easy in Console, but API callers might be impacted. If we make “reason” required at API level it’s a breaking change for scripts.

Chloe Martin: We can do: API supports `reason` optional but strongly recommended, Console requires it (at least for enterprise tenants / prod env). But then audit events are inconsistent.

Fiona McCarthy: For compliance customers, “optional reason” becomes “missing evidence”. My preference: require *some* justification for rollback + apply in production scopes (Hosted prod, Dedicated prod, Private prod). Staging/dev can be optional.

Rafael Mendes: On-call reality: if latency is melting and the only fix is rollback, I don’t want folks blocked by a required Jira link. But I can live with required free text if it’s short and doesn’t slow us down.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: On RBAC: we’re introducing `optimize.config.rollback` + `optimize.config.apply`. If you have rollback permission, you can execute. We can add “break-glass role” for SRE/on-call that can bypass justification requirement? (but then audit must flag it).

Kenji Nakamura: UX proposal:
- In version history, each row has “Rollback” action.
- Click -> modal shows blast radius (scope: customer/region/cluster/route/model) + “Rollback to v123 (created by X on Y)”.
- Required field: “Reason for rollback” (placeholder: “e.g., latency spike after v124; incident INC-1234”).
- Optional: “Link to ticket/incident” field.
- Primary button: “Rollback now”. Secondary: “Cancel”.

Marissa Cole: I like required free text (fast), optional link. But I’m worried about us saying “one-click rollback” externally if there’s a modal + required reason.

Kenji Nakamura: We can still market “one-click” as “one action from the UI” — but copy in-product should be “Rollback” (not “one-click”). The modal is expected guardrail.

Paula Mendes: Also we should not call it “Revert” (ambiguous). “Rollback to version” is explicit.

Dylan Brooks: +1 on “Rollback to version”. For UX, can we prefill the reason field with a template so it’s basically just hit enter?

Kenji Nakamura: Yup. Prefill: “Rolling back to v### due to: ” (cursor at end). We can also remember last reason snippet? Maybe too much.

Chloe Martin: Implementation detail: Console can require reason even if backend doesn’t, but we should still pass it through and emit it in audit event payload.

Fiona McCarthy: Audit event must include reason or a statement that reason was omitted. I would rather not allow omitted in prod. If we do “break-glass”, log `justification_bypassed=true`.

Rafael Mendes: Break-glass should be rare. I’d rather just require a short reason always. In an incident I can type “INC-2217 latency regression” in 2 sec.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC nuance: permission-gated + justification are different controls. We can enforce reason requirement via policy engine: if env=prod AND scope in {Hosted,Dedicated,Private} -> require `reason` non-empty.

Marissa Cole: That seems like the right shape. PRD language: “Rollback is permission-gated and requires operator justification for production applies/rollbacks.”

Paula Mendes: Please also ensure we capture “who/what/where” in the confirmation view. Users keep asking “am I rolling back just my route or the whole customer?”

Kenji Nakamura: Will add blast radius section with explicit bullets:
- Customer: ACME
- Deployment: Dedicated us-east-1 / cluster rwd-ded-23
- Routes: /chat, /embeddings
- Models: llama-3.1-70b
- Change: v124 -> v123

Dylan Brooks: We should add a “View diff” link directly in the modal too. In case you want sanity check what you’re going back to.

Chloe Martin: +1. We already have diff payload for compare view. Modal can show condensed summary + link to full compare.

Marissa Cole: Customer-facing wording: do we say “Known-good versions” anywhere? I worry it implies we guarantee quality.

Fiona McCarthy: “Known-good” is risky legally/expectations. Better: “previous versions” + “last applied successfully”. Those are factual.

Paula Mendes: Agree. In PRD: use “last successfully applied version” and “currently active version”.

Kenji Nakamura: Copy suggestions:
- Section header: “Version history”
- Badge: “Active” on current
- Badge: “Applied successfully” on others (if we track)
- Action: “Rollback”
- Modal title: “Rollback configuration”
- Warning text: “This will replace the active optimization configuration for the selected scope.”

Rafael Mendes: Also add “This may temporarily increase cost/latency while caches warm” if we’re rolling back cache/batch settings? Or too scary?

Dylan Brooks: We can keep modal short and put “Operational notes” behind an info tooltip. Don’t want to block rollbacks with too much text.

Paula Mendes: For enterprise admins, they might actually want that warning. But ok as tooltip + link to runbook.

Marissa Cole: Decision check:
1) Rollback requires `optimize.config.rollback` permission.
2) Prod rollbacks require non-empty reason; ticket link optional.
3) In-product copy: “Rollback” / “Rollback to version v###”, avoid “known-good”.
4) Confirmation modal shows blast radius + link to diff.
Everyone aligned?

Kenji Nakamura: aligned :thumbsup:

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: will reflect in Console flow.

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: will add to API spec: accept `reason` + `links[]` (even if optional for now), and policy enforces prod.

Fiona McCarthy: aligned, please add explicit audit event fields in PRD: `reason`, `ticket_link`, `justification_required`, `justification_provided`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: I’ll sync with Marcus on policy enforcement location (RBAC service vs Console backend). Prefer centralized policy so API is covered.

Rafael Mendes: Works for on-call. Please ensure reason field doesn’t reset if the rollback call fails and user retries.

Marissa Cole: Great call. Adding to UX acceptance criteria. I’ll update PRD section today and link in Linear PM-412.

(Reaction summary: Kenji Nakamura added :eyes: to “blast radius section”; Fiona McCarthy added :lock: to “prod requires reason”; Dylan Brooks added :white_check_mark: to “View diff in modal”.)
